title: Bougainvillea glabra

{{Short description|Species of flowering plant}} {{Speciesbox | image = Bugenwilla.Długo kwitnaca roslina.jpg | status = LC | status_system = IUCN3.1 | status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Botanic Gardens Conservation International (BGCI). |author2=IUCN SSC Global Tree Specialist Group. |year=2019 |title=''Bougainvillea glabra'' |article-number=e.T149207944A149207946 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2019-2.RLTS.T149207944A149207946.en}} | taxon = Bougainvillea glabra | authority = [[Jacques Denis Choisy|Choisy]]{{GRIN | accessdate = 2014-01-30}} | synonyms = {{collapsible list | {{species list |Bougainvillea glabra var. typica |Heimerl |Bougainvillea spectabilis var. glabra |(Choisy) Hook. |Bougainvillea arborea |Glaz. |Bougainvillea brachycarpa |Heimerl |Bougainvillea formosa |W.Bull |Bougainvillea glabra var. acutibracteata |Heimerl/small>
|Bougainvillea glabra var. alba |Mendes & Viégas |Bougainvillea glabra var. brachycarpa |(Heimerl) Heimerl |Bougainvillea glabra var. graciliflora |Heimerl |Bougainvillea glabra var. obtusibracteata |Heimerl |Bougainvillea glabra var. sanderiana |Dimmock |Bougainvillea rubicunda |Schott ex Rohrb. |Bougainvillea sanderiana |(Dimmock) W.Falc.bis }} }} }} '''''Bougainvillea glabra''''', the '''lesser bougainvillea''' or '''paperflower''',[http://eol.org/pages/404392/names/common_names Common names for Lesser Bougainvillea (''Bougainvillea glabra'')—Encyclopedia of Life] is the most common [[species]] of [[bougainvillea]] used for [[bonsai]].{{cite web |url= http://www.bonsai-bci.com/files/Bougainvillea.pdf |title= Bougainvillea bonsai |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140309030224/http://www.bonsai-bci.com/files/Bougainvillea.pdf |archive-date= March 9, 2014 }} {{small|(96 Kb)}} The epithet 'glabra' comes from Latin and means "bald".Yasin J. Nasir: Flora of West Pakistan 115: Nyctaginaceae. Stewart Herbarium, Gordon College (et al.), Rawalpindi 1977, p. 13. == Description == It is an [[evergreen]], climbing [[shrub]] that usually grows {{convert|10|–|12|ft|m|order=flip|round=0.5|abbr=on}} tall, occasionally up to {{convert|30|ft|m|0|abbr=on|order=flip}}. It features thick, thorny [[Plant stem|stems]] and drooping branches that are glabrous or sparsely hairy. The leaves have a {{convert|3-10|mm|in|frac=16|adj=mid|-long}} stem. The [[leaf blade]] is ovate to ovate-lanceolate, pointed or briefly pointed, 5 to 13 centimeters long and 3 to 6 centimeters wide, sparsely fluffy hairy on the underside and bald on the top. The leaf-like [[bracts]] are purple, oblong or elliptical, pointed, {{convert|2+1/2|-|3+1/2|in|mm|order=flip|abbr=on|round=5}} long and about {{convert|2|in|mm|order=flip|abbr=on|round=5}} wide. They tower over the flowers. These grow individually in pairs or in groups of three on flower stems about 3.5 millimeters long.{{citation needed|date=March 2023}} [[Raphide]]s have been found in the stem, bracts and different parts of the flower.{{sfn|Gulliver|1864|p=251}} ===Inflorescences=== The crown tube is greenish, clearly angled, about 2 centimeters long, sparsely downy hairy, ribbed and points away from the [[pedicel (botany)|flower stalk]]. The tip is lobed five times and forms a short, spread, white or yellowish hem. The six to eight stamens have 8 to 13 millimeter long [[stamen]]s. The [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]] is about 2 millimeters long, the stylus 1 millimeter and the scar 2.5 millimeters.Andreas Bärtels: Tropical plants. Ornamental and useful plants. 5th, revised edition. Eugen Ulmer Verlag, Stuttgart 2002, {{ISBN|3-8001-3937-5}}, p. 186 . Tiny white [[flower]]s usually appear in clusters surrounded by colorful papery [[bract]]s, hence the name paperflower. The [[Leaf|leaves]] are dark green, variable in shape, up to {{convert|4|in|mm|round=5|order=flip|abbr=on}} long.{{Cite web |url=http://cals.arizona.edu/pima/gardening/aridplants/Bougainvillea_glabra.html |title=''Bougainvillea glabra'' - University of Arizona Pima County Cooperative Extension |access-date=2007-04-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070428185825/http://cals.arizona.edu/pima/gardening/aridplants/Bougainvillea_glabra.html |archive-date=2007-04-28 }} The flowers are about {{convert|0.4|cm|||abbr=on}} in diameter (the pink petal-like structures are not petals, but bracts).{{cite web|last1=Bougainvillea glabra|title=Bougainvillea glabra|url=https://mybonsaiworld.com/bougainvillea-glabra-bonsai/|website=Bonsai World |date=30 September 2024 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==Cultivation== ''B. glabra'' is heat and drought tolerant and frost sensitive. It is easily [[Plant propagation|propagated]] by [[Cutting (plant)|cuttings]]. It needs full sunlight, warm weather and well drained soil to flower well. The species is often used in culture, in areas with frost in glass houses, otherwise outdoors. The similar ''[[Bougainvillea spectabilis]]'', which differs from ''Bougainvillea glabra'' by the velvety-felty underside of the leaves, is also cultivated, but less frequently.{{citation needed|date=March 2023}} ===Uses=== Being of medical importance, the [[infusion]] of the plant's tender leaves and bracts is used orally to treat gastrointestinal problems (diarrhoea, stomach pain), and [[respiratory condition]]s ([[asthma]], [[bronchitis]], [[catarrh]], [[chest pain]], [[fever]], [[pneumonia]], [[whooping cough]]).Peter Schönfelder, Ingrid Schönfelder: The cosmos-Canary flora.
